<description>
This PR is part of integrating silent payments into Bitcoin Core. It is the second iteration of https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28122, now based on https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1765.

This project is tracked in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/28536.

BIP352
This PR focuses strictly on the BIP logic and attempts to separate it from the wallet and transaction implementation details. This is accomplished by working directly with public and private keys, instead of needing a wallet backend and transactions for testing. Labels for the receiver are optional and thus deferred for a later PR.

Test vectors from the BIP are included as unit tests.
</description>

[2026-09-22] rc:4070468499 inline on src/common/bip352.h by ismaelsadeeq (member) (edited 2026-09-22):
In "common: add bip352.{h,cpp} secp256k1 module" 8fe356913e95dc980a5d115c0ef880c6e04fadd6

Hmm, a default constructed `PrevoutsSummary` is a valid C++ object holding a zeroed summary. The class doesn't enforce "populated by secp before use", so nothing stops someone writing

```c++
bip352::PrevoutsSummary ps;      // zeroed, never filled
receiver.Scan(ps, outputs);      // compiles, silently wrong
```

While I'm here, the type has a few related issues, all from the same thing, it exposes its raw pointer so an outside function can fill it in two phases, but

1. Two-phase init / valid-but-empty state (above): the public default ctor produces an unpopulated object; population happens later, out-of-band.
2. `Get() const` returns a mutable pointer (`secp256k1_silentpayments_prevouts_summary*`). So a `const PrevoutsSummary` hands out a writable pointer to its internals `Scan` takes const `PrevoutsSummary&` but could mutate it. libsecp confirms the two paths differ: `_prevouts_summary_create` wants `T*`,`_scan_outputs` wants `const T*`. The accessor should be `const T*`.

3. The fill logic lives in a detached free function, `CreateInputPubkeysTweak`, which reaches into the object via `Get()`.

I'd suggest a factory that guarantees a valid, immutable value

Make the ctor private and expose only a `static Create` or `From` like  `SilentPaymentDestination` that returns `std::optional`. Then the object is either populated or not at all, and `Get()` can be const-only:

```c++
class PrevoutsSummary
{
    std::unique_ptr<secp256k1_silentpayments_prevouts_summary>

    // Private: allocates empty storage for Create() to fill.
    PrevoutsSummary();

public:
    //! Summarize a transaction's input public keys and smallest outpoint
    //! Returns nullopt if libsecp rejects the inputs.
    static std::optional<PrevoutsSummary> Create(
        const std::vector<CPubKey>& plain_pubkeys,
        const std::vector<XOnlyPubKey>& taproot_pubkeys,
        const COutPoint& smallest_outpoint);

    PrevoutsSummary(PrevoutsSummary&&) noexcept;
    PrevoutsSummary& operator=(PrevoutsSummary&&) noexcept;
    ~PrevoutsSummary();

    const secp256k1_silentpayments_prevouts_summary* Get() const LIFETIMEBOUND;
};
```

This closes all four issues, the object is immutable and the create factory method returns either valid or nullopt.

Also this makes it clearer from the interface what we are summarising.
